visual_message: Gravity accelerates a horizontally launched ball downward. A ball dropped from the same height at the same time has the same vertical motion and reaches the ground together with it.
subject: Gravity
title: One launch. Two motions.
assumptions: Both balls begin at the same height with zero vertical velocity

cues.heading: Watch what happens after launch
cues.text: The cannon gives the ball horizontal motion.

cues.heading: Gravity adds downward motion
cues.text: The ball keeps moving forward as it accelerates downward.

cues.heading: Together, those motions form a curve
cues.text: The trail marks the ball's position at equal time intervals.

cues.heading: Now compare it with a dropped ball
cues.text: Same height. Same release time. Zero initial vertical speed.

cues.heading: Their vertical motion stays the same
cues.text: Moving sideways does not change how quickly either ball falls.

cues.heading: Both reach the ground together
cues.text: From the same height, with air resistance ignored.

acceptance: The launched ball follows the computed parabolic trajectory
The comparison ball drops vertically outside the cannon platform
Both balls have equal height at every comparison instant
Both reach the ground at the same instant
All objects and captions fit landscape and portrait frames
The gravity arrow represents downward acceleration, not a downward-only velocity
